title: unstake performs outbound ERC1155 transfer before tail _recomputeSchedule; read-only reentrancy view-inconsistency window (no in-scope consumer)
description: In unstake (both NFTStaker and the NFTStakerPriceScaled copy) the outbound ERC1155 safeTransferFrom (onERC1155Received on a caller-chosen recipient) executes BEFORE the tail _recomputeSchedule, so during the receive callback totalStaked is already decremented while rewardRate/windowEnd still reflect the OLD pool. Value-reporting views (currentRewardRate/runwaySeconds/totalNFTValue) return a transiently inconsistent snapshot mid-callback. State-changing reentry is blocked by the contract-wide nonReentrant. Impact requires an external oracle-style consumer that prices collateral off these views inside the callback — NONE known in scope.
impact: None demonstrated in scope. Read-only transient view inconsistency during another party's unstake callback; nonReentrant blocks any state-changing reentry. Would only rise above Low if an in-scope consumer/oracle of these views is later introduced. Ceiling-Low (implausible-High) retained for visibility (Law 1 keep-not-drop).
attackPath: 1. Attacker unstakes to an attacker-controlled ERC1155 receiver.
2. Inside onERC1155Received, totalStaked is decremented but rewardRate/windowEnd not yet recomputed -> views read an inconsistent (stale-rate vs new-supply) snapshot.

3. A hypothetical downstream integrator that reads currentRewardRate/runwaySeconds/totalNFTValue during the callback and prices something off it could be misled. No such in-scope consumer exists; nonReentrant blocks any state-changing reentry.
4. (No realized loss without an external victim contract.)
recommendation: Move the outbound ERC1155 transfer AFTER _recomputeSchedule (strict CEI) so the value-reporting views are consistent throughout the receive callback. Re-escalate only if an in-scope oracle/integrator of these views appears.
category: Low / implausible-High read-only reentrancy exposure (no in-scope victim; nonReentrant holds)
